clue.text: An English seductress might know what makes this something for your lips

parts.words: An English seductress might know what makes this
parts.note: surface reading: a temptress who understands what drives British men
setter's reading: what makes British men tick, run together as one word, is a brand of balm for the mouth

explanation.surface: A British femme fatale's secret knowledge, offered as a beauty tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Split CHAPSTICK as CHAP'S TICK: chap is British slang for a man, so a seductress knows what makes chaps tick.
explanation.definitionFit: ChapStick is a well-known brand of lip balm, used generically for any balm stick applied to the mouth.

clue.text: Raise initial grade of physician hoarding flaky mineral for Jim Carrey, for instance

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep stored inside, so one piece holds the other
grades run A, B, C, D, so raising the first letter's grade swaps it for a better one

parts.note: a doctor is a physician
mica is a mineral that splits into thin flakes

explanation.surface: A doctor with a mineral stash promotes a famous funnyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the front of the physician is raised to grade C, and the mineral goes in after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Carrey is a Canadian-American actor famous for slapstick roles, an example of a comedy performer.

clue.text: Manage poorly rated skirts inside

indicators.note: inside means the next piece goes within the other
something done poorly is done badly, so the letters next to it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
minis are short skirts

explanation.surface: A fashion critic gives a dim review of the hemlines on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage poorly' looks like the definition, but poorly belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to run or be in charge of it, a synonym for managing.

clue.text: What leaks from part of a cross-reference

parts.note: the instruction word with which a cross-reference sends the reader elsewhere
the place a cross-reference points to, usually followed by a number

explanation.surface: Something dribbling out of an index entry.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference typically reads 'see page 12'; its first two words run together give the leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid that oozes slowly out through small openings.

clue.text: Comforting words to ski bum

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters before it are put in a broken order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Reassuring a slope-loving drifter after a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: A ski bum is a person who lives to ski, but bum is the anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: It's OK is what one says to reassure or console someone who is upset.

clue.text: Some hawks trek less when disoriented

indicators.note: being disoriented means losing one's bearings, so the letters wander into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Birds of prey travel shorter distances when they lose their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Kestrels are small falcons, and falcons are often loosely grouped among hawks as birds of prey.

clue.text: One radical restrains really, really obscene oil company

indicators.note: to restrain something is to hold it in, so one piece is placed around the other
radical change means a drastic rearrangement, so the letters of the word before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
X is the rating for obscene films; doubling it makes it really, really so

explanation.surface: An extremist objects to an oil firm's sleazy conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of One hold the two Xs between their first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Exxon is a major American petroleum corporation, now part of ExxonMobil.

clue.text: Pose awkwardly to exploit embrace

indicators.note: an awkward pose is clumsily arranged, so the word before it is put in a clumsy new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Striking a clumsy pose in order to take advantage of a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embrace' looks like a hug, but it means adopting a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a belief or cause is to adopt and support it, as one embraces an idea.

clue.text: How to Look Within Ruins (in pig Latin)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scan that lets a doctor see inside the body
second meaning: ruins are wrecks, said like rex, and pig Latin moves the opening R to the end and adds -ay

explanation.walkthrough: Pig Latin is an English children's word game: move a word's opening consonant to the end and add -ay. The capitals pretend the first part is a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray image shows the bones within, and 'ex-ray' is how rex, the sound of wrecks, comes out in pig Latin.

clue.text: Whether you look up or down, both hands point up now

indicators.text: Whether you look up or down
indicators.note: a down entry read upward or downward giving the same word tells us it reads the same both ways

parts.words: Whether you look up or down
parts.note: surface reading: glancing up or down at a clock
setter's reading: the hour of the day when a clock's two hands are together at twelve

explanation.surface: Checking the clock face at midday, whichever way you glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry is a down light, so 'up or down' refers to reading it in either direction; the word is the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: At midday the hour and minute hands both sit on twelve, pointing straight up.

clue.text: Coal in Mississippi is an arm and a leg

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: MS is the postal abbreviation for Mississippi
an ember is a glowing piece of coal

explanation.surface: Mississippi coal is fearsomely expensive, costing an arm and a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An arm and a leg' is an idiom for a high price, but here it is read literally as two limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs of the body are called members, so an arm and a leg are two of them.

clue.text: Singer's conciliatory gift drove band

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or appease
drove, as in ran a vehicle or business
a band is a ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A vocalist's peace offering was driving the group around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' is 'Singer is', the definition followed by the wordplay. 'Band' looks like a musical group, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest vocal range, an example of the defined class.

clue.text: Is unable to secure our group on the radio — difficult!

indicators.note: anything heard on the radio is heard, not seen, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.words: Is unable to secure our group
parts.note: is unable is can't, to secure is to anchor, and our group is us

explanation.surface: A broadcaster complains that it can't get the band settled for the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantankerous person is bad-tempered and argumentative, so hard to deal with.

clue.text: Be judged and processed last, darn it

indicators.note: something processed is broken down and reworked, so the letters that follow come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A defendant grumbles about having their case heard at the end of the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' fits the legal picture of being booked, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand trial is to have one's case heard and judged in a court of law.

clue.text: Yellow bench found amid more hackneyed author's equipment, sometimes

indicators.note: something found amid another thing is in its middle, so it goes inside

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, so triter is more so
Y is an abbreviation for yellow
a pew is a church bench

explanation.surface: A cowardly seat discovered among an ever more clichéd writer's things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' reads as cowardly, but here it is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Many writers once produced their manuscripts on a typewriter, and some still do.

clue.text: Nutcase conceals height and weight

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide something within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the back half of the word, taken as written; its front half is the definition
H is the standard abbreviation for height
W is an abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A lunatic is cagey about how tall and heavy he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutcase' looks like one word for a crazy person, but it splits into the definition and the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is the kidney-shaped edible seed of a tropical tree, sold as a nut.

clue.text: It might keep you in bed: a Streisand movie whose opening has shifted to the end with ease

indicators.text: whose opening has shifted to the end
indicators.note: the first letter of the title is moved from the front to the back before it joins on

parts.words: It might keep you in bed
parts.note: influenza is an illness that confines you to bed
Yentl is Barbra Streisand's 1983 film, its first letter moved to the end

explanation.surface: A long-winded remark about a sick-day film that drags on.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something fluently is to do it smoothly and without effort, chiefly said of speech.

clue.text: A bit of bread stuffing left on the plate without a loss

indicators.note: stuffing something means filling its inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: food left on the plate has not been eaten

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: the leading letter of bread

explanation.surface: A crust of bread in the stuffing goes uneaten, nothing wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like the food in the scene, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that is unbeaten has not lost a single game.

clue.text: Implicit connotation of person who lacks subtlety

parts.note: lacking subtlety means being open and blatant
one can stand for a person, as in 'one who'

explanation.surface: A tactless person's remarks carry an unintended hidden meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the blatant person spells out a word for the very opposite: a meaning that is only hinted at.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a suggested secondary meaning or feeling beneath what is said outright.

clue.text: For example, article not returned with shipping tax

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
an is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: An item is sent back because of a shipping duty, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not returned' tempts you to keep the item in place; in fact all three pieces are turned around together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage was historically a duty levied on ships according to their cargo capacity in tons.

clue.text: South of the border, 15 fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the number fifteen in Spanish, the language spoken south of the US border
second meaning: a hard, pear-shaped fruit used in jams

explanation.walkthrough: '15' looks like a reference to the clue 15-across, but it is just the number, translated into Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Quince is Spanish for fifteen, and in English it names a yellow, fragrant fruit related to the apple.

clue.text: Improvement to fix rude gap

indicators.note: fixing something means working it over, so the letters that follow are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Renovating to repair an ugly hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An upgrade raises something to a higher standard, so it is a betterment.

clue.text: Researcher put resources on one reptile

parts.note: to invest is to put money or resources into something
I is the Roman numeral for one
gator is short for alligator

explanation.surface: A scientist pours funding into studying a single reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator looks into things systematically, as a researcher does.

clue.text: Cast is terminated at an audition

definitions.note: the sound-alike of the answer means terminated

parts.note: first meaning: tossed or flung

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is judged by sound

parts.note: terminated means finished, or through

explanation.surface: An actor learns they're dropped from the production during tryouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'audition' paint a theatre scene, but cast is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast and threw are both past tenses of verbs for flinging something.

clue.text: Dance for a bit of money

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here only its opening letter

parts.note: pro means for, in favor of
the opening letter of money

explanation.surface: Someone will dance if paid a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a formal dance held for high-school students, especially in the US.

clue.text: Irritable executives don't get yogurt on their faces

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so each of the preceding words contributes its first letter

parts.note: the leading letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Cranky bosses are spared a dessert in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a food fight, but only the faces, the first letters, of four words count.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone edgy is tense and nervous, quick to become irritated.

clue.text: Go back to the drawing board with a colorful bunch

definitions.text: Go back to the drawing board

parts.note: red is a color
a raft is a large number or collection, as in a raft of ideas
the article joins with the next word

explanation.surface: An artist restarts a design with a vivid group of colors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A raft of' means a lot of, so a bunch is a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to write a new version of something, starting a plan over again.

clue.text: Practical thinker about top celebrities

parts.note: re means about, as in a memo heading
the A-list is the most celebrated people

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth person muses on the biggest stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist sees situations as they are and acts sensibly, a pragmatic person.

clue.text: Head of Microsoft blasted eBay, perhaps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the leading letter of the company name

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters that follow land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Microsoft's boss attacks a rival tech company, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eBay, perhaps' reads as an example of a website, but 'perhaps' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are interchangeable adverbs expressing possibility.

clue.text: Economic reformer listening to naked fisherman

indicators.note: when you are listening to something you take in how it sounds, not how it is spelled

parts.note: naked is nude, and a fisherman catching eels is an eeler

explanation.surface: A financial reformer tunes in to a nudist angler.
explanation.walkthrough: A New Dealer backed Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal economic programs of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Deal was a sweeping reform of the US economy, so its supporters were economic reformers.
